newsitem.title: GERMANY: German court rejects Seles damages claim.
newsitem.headline: German court rejects Seles damages claim.

text.p: A German court on Thursday rejected a damages suit brought by tennis star Monica Seles against the German Tennis Federation over security measures at a tournament where she was stabbed in 1993.

Lawyers for Seles had claimed 24.4 million marks ($15.75 million) for lost earnings during her 27-month layoff after the attack at the Hamburg Open event. They had claimed security at the tournament was lax.
The court gave no immediate explanation for its decision but ruled Seles would have to pay the costs of the trial.

The U.S. star's lawyers had claimed the players' bench in the stadium was too close to the spectators' stand, from where lathe operator Guenter Parche leapt to stab Seles in the back with a kitchen knife in April 1993.
Parche was given a two-year suspended sentence in October 1993 for grievous bodily harm. The trial judge ruled he was emotionally retarded and may not have been entirely responsible for his actions.

Prosecutors had asked the court to jail Parche for attempted murder. A subsequent appeal by Seles for a harder sentence failed. Parche said at the time he wanted to wound Seles out of love for her German rival, Steffi Graf.
